FINDING_ID: IM_F001  
SEVERITY: 0.96  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.93  
DESCRIPTION: `process_round()` uses two incompatible notions of who was supposed to answer. Area 6 failure handling only iterates actual `responses` in [dynamic_management.py:5045](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L5045), but the immune feed later iterates the entire model pool and treats `mid not in responses` as a failure in [dynamic_management.py:5153](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L5153). Because `FailureHandler.should_abort()` depends on `_active_models`, which only changes through recovery handling in [dynamic_management.py:4419](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L4419), a model that simply never appears in `responses` can evade Area 6 failure handling entirely, while excluded or intentionally unassigned models can be falsely accumulated as immune “model failures.” The real defect is the missing “expected responders” contract between dispatch/allocation and the Response layer.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Change `process_round()` to accept the expected responder set for the round, ideally from the actual allocation. Use that same set for both failure detection and immune per-model tracking. For expected-but-missing responders, synthesize an explicit missing-response failure; for inactive or unassigned models, skip failure and immune tracking entirely.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F002  
SEVERITY: 0.92  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.88  
DESCRIPTION: A remediation rejected by P-pass is still recorded as if a fix had been applied. In [dynamic_management.py:5872](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L5872), `apply_diagnosis()` mutates or creates `_remediation_state` even when `proceed` is false, and `_verify_remediation_outcomes()` later treats every `_remediation_state` entry as a real applied remediation in [dynamic_management.py:3053](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L3053). That means natural metric drift can be misreported as a successful fix that never actually ran, and step-effectiveness/self-diagnosis statistics become contaminated by phantom interventions.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Do not create or advance `remediation_state` for rejected steps. Record rejected P-pass decisions in a separate log or deferred queue, and only create verification state after a transform has actually been applied.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F003  
SEVERITY: 0.87  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.79  
DESCRIPTION: Human-approved deferred remediations are applied through a separate path that backdates the change and skips normal safety bookkeeping. In [dynamic_management.py:5949](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L5949), `approve_deferred_remediation()` records the adjustment and verification state using the original diagnosis round instead of the actual approval/apply round. It also bypasses the pre-fix regression snapshot path used by AUTO remediations in [dynamic_management.py:5888](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L5888). If approval happens later, damping and verification windows are measured from the wrong time, and regressions from approved fixes are invisible to the regression detector.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Make approval take the current round index and route approved fixes through the same post-apply helper as AUTO fixes: capture a pre-fix snapshot, record the adjustment with the real apply round, and set remediation state from that same round.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F004  
SEVERITY: 0.80  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.70  
DESCRIPTION: The Response telemetry contract is internally inconsistent. `ManagerEventType` defines `FORMAT_VIOLATION`, `UNDERPERFORM`, and recovery event types in [dynamic_management.py:4668](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L4668), but `detect_failure()` emits `MALFORMED` for format failures in [dynamic_management.py:4300](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L4300), emits no event at all for underperformance in [dynamic_management.py:4312](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L4312), and there are no recovery-event emission sites anywhere in the module. Downstream monitoring therefore cannot reliably distinguish parse failures, format failures, underperformance, or actual recovery actions, despite the enum and interface comments claiming that it can.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Emit `FORMAT_VIOLATION` and `UNDERPERFORM` from `detect_failure()`, and emit explicit recovery events after `get_recovery()` selects an action. Add tests that assert event types, not just returned `FailureType` values.  
VERIFIED: TRUE
